transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, my sister actually made the appointment for me, because honestly, my body just feels completely out of my control lately, like I'm not even the one driving it anymore. A few weeks ago, I was just... I couldn't stop moving. I was pacing around my apartment, literally all night long, back and forth, back and forth, from the kitchen to the living room. I work as a waiter right now, but I was up making all these incredibly detailed notes for this underground supper-club I was going to start, writing down menus and seating charts until the sun came up, and I just had this electricity in my limbs, you know? I couldn't sit still if you paid me. But then, I don't even know when it shifted, but lately... lately it's the exact opposite. I feel like I'm moving through molasses. My sister came over the other day to take me to the grocery store because I haven't been going, and she was just standing by the door, and she said, "It is taking you forever just to put your shoes on." And she was right, I was just staring at my sneakers, and my hands felt so heavy, like lead, and just tying the laces felt like this massive, exhausting task. It's just so bizarre to go from vibrating out of my skin to barely being able to lift my feet.
During that time when you were pacing and making all those plans, did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual?

I mean... I don't really know if 'needed' is the right word, or if I even thought about it like that. I'm honestly not sure. I just... I was just awake, you know? Like, I wasn't looking at the clock thinking about my sleep schedule at all. I don't really remember feeling one way or the other about my actual need for it. 

I was just so intensely focused on the menus. I remember I had this whole concept for a five-course tasting menu based on, like, obscure childhood nostalgia, and I was trying to figure out how to source edible marigolds and this specific type of heirloom tomato at three in the morning. And my apartment—I live in this older building near the college—it has this really awful fluorescent lighting in the kitchen, the kind that kind of hums constantly and makes everything look washed out and yellow? So I was just standing under that humming light, leaning against the laminate counter, just writing and writing on these yellow legal pads I found, and the time just sort of vanished entirely. 

So I couldn't tell you if my body actually required less sleep, or if I just completely forgot that sleep was even a thing a person was supposed to do. My roommate, Dave, he actually came out to get a glass of water at one point and just stared at me, but I just kept talking to him about the marigold sourcing until he finally just shook his head and went back to bed. So, yeah, I really couldn't say for sure if I felt like I needed less of it... I just wasn't really doing it.
During that time when you were making all those plans, did you feel unusually powerful or especially capable, like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yeah... yeah, I actually really did. It’s almost embarrassing to say out loud now, sitting here, but at the time, I was absolutely convinced I had this... this genius vision. I mean, I was literally just working as a waiter at this average Italian place, taking orders for chicken parm, but in my head, I was a visionary. I honestly believed I was about to build the best bilingual supper club in the entire city. Like, I had this whole concept where the menus would be in English and Spanish, and the dishes would bridge these two culinary worlds in a way no one had ever thought of before. 

I was so sure of it, I thought it was just a matter of time before the money rolled in. I remember thinking that investors would be incredibly stupid not to back me. Like, they would be missing out on the opportunity of a lifetime if they didn't throw money at me. I didn't even have a job lined up that could fund it, I definitely didn't have any savings, and I had absolutely zero connections to anyone with that kind of capital. My bank account was basically empty. But none of that mattered. I just felt this absolute certainty, this raw power, like I was untouchable and everything I touched was going to turn to gold. I was walking around thinking I was the smartest person in any room, that I was just operating on this entirely different frequency than everyone else, including Dave, who just couldn't see the brilliance of what I was doing with the marigolds. It was like I had this secret knowledge, this supreme capability that no one else had.
During this recent slowed-down period, have you been feeling depressed most of the day?

I mean, I don't really know if "depressed" is the right word for it. It's more just... I don't know, it's like I'm just existing, you know? Like I said, I'm just so slowed down, everything is just taking so much effort. I'm not sitting around crying all day or feeling sad, necessarily, I'm just... empty. It's like the volume on my entire life has been turned all the way down to zero. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to go into work for a lunch shift. I actually really like the lunch crowd, it's usually older people, regulars who tip well and don't make a fuss. But I woke up, and I just stared at the ceiling for... I don't even know, maybe three hours? Just looking at this one water stain that's been there since I moved in, and I just couldn't find a single reason to care about getting up. I wasn't sad about the water stain, I wasn't sad about missing work, I just felt absolutely nothing. I ended up calling out, which I hate doing because my manager, Gary, he's actually a really decent guy and he always tries to give me the good sections, but I just couldn't do it. 

And it's not just work, it's everything. I haven't even looked at my supper club notes in days. They're just sitting there on the kitchen counter, next to the toaster, and I look at them and I just feel this complete blankness. So, I don't know if that's what you mean by depressed, but it's definitely not how I usually feel. It's just this heavy, blank feeling all day long.
During that energized time, did you have any experiences that other people said weren’t real, like hearing voices or believing something unusual with absolute certainty?

I mean, no, nothing like that. No voices or anything. I wasn't hallucinating or seeing things that weren't there, if that's what you mean. I know some people get like that, but that wasn't me. I mean, sure, I was absolutely convinced about the supper club, like I was saying before, I really believed it was this million-dollar idea and that I was this culinary genius, but it wasn't like I thought I was, I don't know, receiving messages from God about the marigolds or something. It was just a really, really intense belief in myself and my own ideas. 

I remember Dave, my roommate, he did tell me I was acting crazy. He literally used that word, "crazy." It was that night I was up at 3 AM under the fluorescent lights, and he came out for water. He was just standing there in his boxers, rubbing his eyes, and I was going on and on about how I was going to revolutionize the dining scene in the city, and he just looked at me and said, "Dude, you're acting crazy, you need to go to sleep." But he didn't mean I was seeing ghosts or hearing voices. He just meant I was being way too intense about a restaurant concept when I didn't even have a business degree or any money. 

So, yeah, I never heard voices or thought the government was after me or anything bizarre like that. It was all just very grounded in my own reality, just... a really amplified version of it, I guess. I was just really, really focused on the menus and the sourcing and the bilingual aspect of it all. I mean, the bilingual thing alone, I had this whole plan to have the waitstaff switch seamlessly between languages depending on the table, which I still think is a pretty solid idea, honestly, even if the execution was a little... rushed in my head at the time. But no, no voices or anything like that. Just me and my own very loud thoughts.
At any point during that energized period, were you also feeling that same heavy, empty, slowed-down state at the same time?

No, no, definitely not. It was like... they were two completely different worlds, you know? Like night and day. When I was in that energized zone, working on the supper club, figuring out the whole bilingual menu concept and the marigold sourcing... I mean, I was flying. There was absolutely no heaviness, no emptiness. I was literally buzzing with energy, like I had electricity running through my veins instead of blood. I felt so light and fast, like I could run a marathon and then immediately cook a five-course meal for fifty people without breaking a sweat. 

I wasn't feeling slowed down at all. I was the exact opposite. I was moving so fast, talking so fast, thinking so fast. Dave actually told me I was exhausting to be around because I just wouldn't stop moving or talking about the restaurant. And I certainly didn't feel empty. I felt... full. Like, completely stuffed with ideas and plans and this absolute certainty that I was going to succeed. 

It wasn't until... well, later, when all that energy just vanished, that the heavy, blank feeling started. It was like someone just flipped a switch and suddenly the power was out. But they definitely didn't happen at the same time. When I was up, I was completely up. And when I crashed and started staring at that water stain for hours... that's when the emptiness hit. So, no, they never overlapped. It was one extreme or the other.
About how many days did that energized period last?

Days? Oh, no, no, it wasn't just a few days. I mean, if it was just a weekend, Dave wouldn't have been nearly as annoyed with me. No, it didn't just flash by like that. Actually, this has been going on for about four months, starting after I got fired from the restaurant. 

Not the place I'm at now with Gary, obviously, but my old job at this upscale bistro downtown. I still say that firing was completely unjustified, by the way. The head chef there, he was always on my case just because I suggested tweaking the plating on their sea bass—which, honestly, looked a little sloppy and rushed—and he just had this massive ego about it. So they let me go, and you'd think I would have been devastated, right? Most people would be crying, stressing about rent, immediately scrambling to print out resumes. But me? That very afternoon, I walked out of those double doors, and it was like a rocket went off in my brain. I just thought, "I don't need them, I can do this so much better myself."

And that's exactly when the supper club idea was born. That energy, that absolute buzzing feeling I was telling you about? It just stayed. For about four entire months, I was operating on that exact same high frequency. Four months of barely sleeping, four months of sketching out floor plans on napkins, four months of researching wholesale prices for edible flowers and trying to find a supplier for the marigolds who wouldn't overcharge me for overnight shipping. It just kept going and going. 

I'd be up at dawn, redesigning the logo for the fifth time, and then I'd be walking around the city for hours looking at vacant commercial spaces I couldn't even afford, just peering through the dusty windows and picturing exactly where the bilingual
During this slowed-down period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, completely. It's honestly one of the weirdest parts of all this, because... well, you know how passionate I am about things. But right now? The stuff that usually keeps me steady, it all just feels completely flat. 

Like, cooking, obviously, is my whole life. You heard how obsessed I was with the supper club and the menus. But lately, I can't even bring myself to boil a pot of water for pasta. And my food photography—I used to take these incredibly detailed food photos for my Instagram. I mean, I'd spend twenty minutes just getting the natural light right on a plate, adjusting the angles, making sure the microgreens looked perfectly crisp before I even took a bite. Now? I haven't opened the app in weeks. I look at a plate of food and it's just... a chore. There's no joy in it.

And it’s not just the food stuff, it’s everything else, too. Music used to be huge for me. I had playlists for prep work, playlists for riding the bus, playlists for winding down. Now I just sit in my room in total silence. Dave, my roommate, he even tried to get me to go to our usual pickup soccer game on Sundays down at the park. We've been playing with the exact same guys for like two years, and I'm always the one hyping everyone up in the group chat on Saturday nights. But last Sunday, he was standing at the door with his cleats on, jingling his keys, and I just stared at him from the couch. I knew I should want to go. Logically, I know I love playing soccer. But I just felt absolutely nothing. 

Even the volunteering I do... I usually help out at this community garden twice a month, which is actually where I first got the idea for sourcing the marigolds locally, but I just haven't shown up. The organizer texted me asking if I was okay, and I couldn't even type back a reply. It's just... it's like I know in my head that I used to care about all these things, I know they make up who I am, but I just can't make myself actually feel it right now. It's just dead air.

I mean, I'd spend twenty minutes just getting the natural light right on a plate, adjusting the angles, making sure the microgreens looked perfectly crisp before I even took a bite. Now? I haven't opened the app in weeks. I look at a plate of food and it's just... a chore. There's no joy in it.

And it’s not just the food stuff, it’s everything else, too. Music used to be huge for me. I had playlists for prep work, playlists for riding the bus, playlists for winding down. Now I just sit in my room in total silence. Dave, my roommate, he even tried to get me to go to our usual pickup soccer game on Sundays down at the park. We've been playing with the exact same guys for like two years, and I'm always the one hyping everyone up in the group chat on Saturday nights. But last Sunday, he was standing at the door with his cleats on, jingling his keys, and I just stared at him from the couch. I knew I should want to go. Logically, I know I love playing soccer. But I just felt absolutely nothing. 

Even the volunteering I do... I usually help out at this community garden twice a month, which is actually where I first got the idea for sourcing the marigolds locally, but I just haven't shown up. The organizer texted me asking if I was okay, and I couldn't even type back a reply. It's just... it's like I know in my head that I used to care about all these things, I know they make up who I am, but I just can't make myself actually feel it right now. It's just dead air.
